plain_english_policy: This bill is a joint resolution (HJR) that does not change Alabama state law or allocate state funds directly. Instead, it serves as an official legislative statement urging the U.S. Congress to fully fund the federal Resource Conservation and Development (RCD) Program in fiscal year 2011 and all subsequent years.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would produce no direct change in Alabama's legal code or budget, but it formally records the legislature's position supporting continued federal funding for local conservation initiatives. It directs state legislators to advocate with their U.S. Congressional delegation on this issue.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors affirmatively advanced the bill by listing themselves as Representatives supporting the resolution to urge federal funding for RCD Councils. The text explicitly states these councils are composed of volunteers including local officials and serve unmet community needs.
evidence_quotes: "WHEREAS, the Resource Conservation and Development (RCD) Program is funded in the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) budget of the United States Department of Agriculture;"
"WHEREAS, RCD Councils are non-profit entities which meet otherwise unmet needs in local communities;"

"BE IT RESOLVED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF ALABAMA... That we urge the U.S. Congress to support full funding of the RCD Program in the 2011 fiscal year budget and each fiscal year budget thereafter so that the vital services of the Resource Conservation and Development Program will continue."
"RESOLVED FURTHER, That a copy of this resolution be provided to each member of the Alabama Congressional Delegation as an indication of our strong sentiment and commitment on this issue"
